svg.title: The Dnieper Line
svg.desc: Situation map covering 30.2°E to 38.4°E, 44.1°N to 48.7°N. Where a river became the front, and what sits on each bank. Areas of control in 1 classes: Russian-occupied (approx.). Schematic polygons drawn by hand from open-source reporting, not a geocoded dataset. Every zone is drawn as assessed control from open-source reporting; no claimed-only or reported-only ground is shown separately. Natural Earth basemap; the Kakhovka Reservoir is drawn as former (drained after the dam breach of 6 June 2023). Positions as of ~2024 · illustrative, not operational intelligence. 1 mapped features can be reached with the Tab key, each one naming what it is. The map draws the assessment it was given; it does not verify who holds what.

path.aria-label: Ukrainian government control, 57% of the mapped area

g.aria-label: Note 1. Kherson, retaken in November 2022. The river has been the line since.
g.title: Kherson, retaken in November 2022. The river has been the line since.

g.aria-label: Note 2. The Kakhovka dam, breached in June 2023. The reservoir behind it drained in a fortnight.
g.title: The Kakhovka dam, breached in June 2023. The reservoir behind it drained in a fortnight.

g.aria-label: Note 3. Europe's largest nuclear plant, occupied since March 2022.
g.title: Europe's largest nuclear plant, occupied since March 2022.

g.aria-label: Note 4. Robotyne: the furthest the 2023 counteroffensive reached.
g.title: Robotyne: the furthest the 2023 counteroffensive reached.
